subject: Rehearsal: temporary non-preemptive slate + handoff window request
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Natalie Chen <natalie@stratos.io>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rehearsal: temporary non-preemptive slate + handoff window request

Hi team — looping you in early. Stratos is asking for a short, predictable rehearsal ahead of the June rollout where we run a full canary + handoff flow that mirrors their production traffic (spike profiles included). They want a clean 3-hour non-preemptive window where we can run:

- end-to-end canary (service-to-service)
- KV/cache warm-up and prefix replay
- failover handoff to fallback model variant

What I'm requesting from Capacity/Ops: a dedicated slate (non-preemptible) for the rehearsal on Friday 28 May, 10:00–13:00 PT. Rough spec in the attached resource_request_table.xlsx but TL;DR: 8x A100-equivalent slots, single region (us-west-2), guaranteed no preemption for the window.

Why this matters: this is the closest simulation we can run to the real cutover. If we discover an autoscale or shard-hotspot behavior that would cause a production outage, we want to catch it now. Stratos will also run a short traffic replay and have their SRE join the incident channel.

Questions for Ops:
- Is an ad-hoc non-preemptive slice for 3 hours feasible without impacting committed Dedicated tenants?
- If we can’t make it fully non-preemptive, what are the explicit degradation modes (throttling vs eviction) and SLO impact?
- Cost/chargeback estimate for the 3-hour window (so we can get commercial sign-off)

I attached a short runbook and the resource ask. Marcus — can you confirm the test plan and number of parallel requests? Natalie — thanks for flagging this early; please confirm Stratos can move the rehearsal if capacity forces us to a backup date.

Thanks — chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Natalie Chen <natalie@stratos.io>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rehearsal: temporary non-preemptive slate + handoff window request

Chloe — thanks for the detailed ask and attachments. Quick answers while I validate cluster-level constraints: 

1) Feasibility: possible but depends on active reservations for the same physical pool. We have a committed Dedicated block running nightly jobs that start around 00:00 UTC on weekdays; the 10:00–13:00 PT window typically has lighter usage but we need to check Qs for the week of 24 May. I’ll run a utilization sweep and confirm by EOD tomorrow.

2) Degradation modes: if we cannot provide a true non-preemptive slice, we can offer a "soft-guard" instead — guaranteed scheduling priority + eviction protection for the first 90 minutes, then best-effort for the remaining time. That would require an autoscale policy exception so the scheduler does not reassign those slots mid-window. The tradeoff is increased risk to bursty shared tenants; we’d want a lead from Product to own rollback triggers.

3) Cost estimate: ballpark on 8x A100 equivalent for 3 hours is ~ $5,400 (raw infra) plus staging-run overhead. We’ll produce a formal chargeback line item once the exact topology is confirmed.

Action items: I’ll post the utilization report and a proposed exception ticket ID. Marcus — can you confirm the exact concurrency and whether we need persistent KV across the window (that changes the memory footprint)?


Kimberly
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Natalie Chen <natalie@stratos.io>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rehearsal: temporary non-preemptive slate + handoff window request

Thanks — quick clarifications from Product/SRE side:

- Concurrency: we expect ~1,800 qps peak for 15 minutes during the replay; sustained ~400 qps for the rest of the window.
- KV persistence: yes, we need prefix replay and persistent KV for the warm-up; that means we should reserve for the full 3 hours not just the spike.
- Rollback trigger: if p50 latency increases >200ms for a sustained 10-minute window, we abort and fall back to the smaller model variant. Chloe and I will be on the incident channel to sign off.

If Kimberly’s soft-guard is the only viable path, we accept the 90-minute guaranteed protection + best-effort tail, but only if we can request an automated graceful drain after the 90-minute mark (not abrupt eviction). We’ll also accept a reduced spec of 6x slots if capacity doesn’t permit 8. Can we get a final decision by EOD Wednesday 19 May so we can lock the runbook and notify Stratos?

Marcus
Group PM, Inference Latency
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie@stratos.io>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rehearsal: temporary non-preemptive slate + handoff window request

Chloe / team — after running the utilization sweep and talking to on-call, here’s what Ops can commit to: 

- Approved exception: a reserved slate for Fri 28 May, 10:00–13:00 PT with the following constraints:
  * Guaranteed protection for the first 90 minutes (10:00–11:30 PT). After 11:30 we will initiate a graceful drain over 15 minutes and then move to best-effort scheduling for the remaining 45 minutes. No immediate evictions during the drain window.
  * If capacity is tight, we will reduce to 6 A100-equivalent slots; we’ll alert by 21 May if that’s required.
  * Autoscale exception ticket created: EXC-2027-1173 (internal).

- Chargeback estimate: $5,200 for 8 slots / 3 hours; $4,000 for 6 slots / 3 hours. Final invoice to be posted to billing once the run occurs.

Next steps: Kimberly will attach the utilization report to EXC-2027-1173. Chloe / Marcus please update the runbook with the rollback trigger and the graceful-drain steps. Natalie — does this work for Stratos or do you need the full non-preemptive guarantee?

Thanks — Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
